claims.text: Increasing chemical short-range order raises the yield strength of multi-component concentrated alloys.
Chemical short-range order preferentially impedes screw-dislocation glide.
Screw-dislocation glide is impeded through formation of diffuse antiphase boundaries.
Short-range order leaves edge-dislocation mobility largely unaffected.
MoNbTaW-type alloys can provide a single-phase BCC, nominally random initial state for the comparison.
Controlled annealing can promote short-range order without causing macroscopic phase separation or precipitation.
Increasing short-range order increases the energy cost of screw-dislocation motion because glide breaks local chemical order.
The additional energy cost of disrupting short-range order requires extra stress for double-kink nucleation.
Edge dislocations are less affected by short-range order than screw dislocations or may have slightly enhanced mobility.
Short-range order shifts plastic deformation toward greater dependence on the impeded screw-dislocation component.
Induced short-range order will increase macroscopic yield strength by approximately 150–200 MPa relative to the random baseline.
Induced short-range order will reduce screw-dislocation mobility relative to the random baseline.
Rapid quenching from the melt preserves a nominally random solid solution with minimal short-range order.
The proposed strengthening mechanism should operate from room temperature to approximately 600 K.
The mechanism should govern single-phase BCC concentrated alloys with comparable valence-electron concentrations.
The mechanism may not govern alloys in which precipitates or secondary phases dominate deformation.
The magnitude of strengthening and the balance of screw and edge activity depend on the degree of short-range order achieved.
Prior evidence shows a strong strengthening effect of short-range order on screw dislocations in MoNbTaW.
